overrideReason: All 3 automated attempts failed. Attempt 1 correctly flagged a real design weakness: its 'cross-vendor seam check' reused the exact same OKX endpoint the backfill used, which the story's own title explicitly rules out as not a genuine seam check - a same-endpoint replay proves nothing about a splice, per research's own blind-spot finding. Attempts 2-3 hit 'not judged - a cheaper layer already failed' against a real, reproducible offline test failure (not an infra flake): test_backfilled_overlap_matches_fresh_independent_live_endpoint_value asserted `backfill_endpoint` contained 'stablecoincharts/Ethereum' but the persisted row's endpoint was the LIVE stablecoinchains URL instead. Investigating this directly (rather than assuming the test was wrong) found a real, previously undiscovered production defect: DefiLlamaStablecoinSupplyOk (used by both the live fetcher and backfill_defillama_stablecoin_supply) has no endpoint field at all, so persist_board's duck-typed getattr(result, 'endpoint', None) fallback always resolved to the registry's static (live) endpoint - every backfilled DefiLlama row silently misrepresented its own provenance. Checked SosoValueEtfFlowOk and BackfilledAlternativeMeFearGreedOk for the same class of gap and found both affected identically (SoSoValue's registry endpoint hardcodes symbol=BTC&limit=1, so a backfilled ETH row would show the wrong asset AND the wrong limit; alternative.me's registry endpoint is ?limit=1 while backfill genuinely calls ?limit=0, a different URL). Fixed all three by adding an optional endpoint field (None for live, explicitly set for backfill) and populating it at each backfill call site. Re-running the fixed test then surfaced a second, more serious defect: DefiLlamaStablecoinChartEntry's extra='forbid' schema rejected every real /stablecoincharts/{chain} response outright, because the vendor's actual response includes totalCirculating, totalMintedUSD, and (on recent entries) totalUnreleased/totalBridgedToUSD - none declared in the schema. This meant the entire DefiLlama backfill recipe was 100% non-functional against real live data despite every offline, fixture-based test passing, since no fixture ever included these real extra fields. Fixed by changing DefiLlamaStablecoinChartEntry to extra='allow' (matching the sibling DefiLlamaPeggedAmounts model's own established tolerance for this vendor's many currency/derived fields), keeping date and totalCirculatingUSD - the only field this project reads - strictly required and typed. Verified live: backfill_defillama_stablecoin_supply now returns 7002 real historical values across all three chains without error. Added a genuine live seam-check test (test_live_backfilled_and_live_defillama_endpoints_agree_at_the_real_seam) hitting the real /stablecoincharts (backfill) and /stablecoinchains (live) endpoints independently - trimmed to a 5-day window via a wrapped recipe so the real API call and real persist path both run, without paying for all ~7000 historical rows. It passed cleanly (20s) against real data. US-909-C1 (sparse-history determinism) and US-909-C3 (board_read origin-filter re-confirmation) were already passing in every attempt and remain so. Full local suite verified clean on current HEAD: uv run mypy ingest --strict clean, uv run ruff check clean, uv run pytest -q -m "not integration" 399 passed, npm --prefix web run typecheck clean, npm --prefix web test 70/70 passed. US-909-C4 is the story's own [human] criterion and is explicitly left for the owner's separate G6_HUMAN judgement - this verdict covers only the three machine-checkable criteria.

results.note: tests/test_backfill_seam.py::test_backfill_run_cannot_splice_a_historical_value_into_current_board_views passes: a registry entry with exactly one persisted row deterministically renders the insufficient-history state, never a fabricated line.

tests/test_backfill_seam.py::test_live_backfilled_and_live_defillama_endpoints_agree_at_the_real_seam PASSED against the real, independent /stablecoincharts and /stablecoinchains DefiLlama endpoints - not a same-endpoint replay - confirming they agree within ordinary intraday drift for the same chain. This test's own construction found and required fixing two real production defects (the missing-endpoint provenance bug and the DefiLlama schema rejecting all real live data) before it could pass at all.

note: 4 of 4 criteria now met. US-909-C4 (the story's [human] criterion) was judged by the owner directly via G6_HUMAN-7f3a91e2 after a real production backfill populated genuine multi-year history (BTC MVRV spanning 2010-07-18 to present). This story's real path to done required finding and fixing three genuine, previously undiscovered production defects (a three-vendor provenance-misattribution bug and a schema defect making DefiLlama's entire backfill recipe non-functional against live data) - none of which any offline, fixture-based test could have caught, exactly the class of finding this project's live-testing discipline exists to require before a genuine [integration:] criterion can be called done.
